Multiply the screen selector at $0200 by three and patch the displacement at $0426 to select a JMP trampoline.
The signed BNE displacement is set to three times the screen index at $0422.
Dispatch selector zero to $0E4F, the sales office menu and its action loop.
Dispatch selector one to $1BDF using the track index in $0216.
Dispatch selector two to the garage handler at $180A.
Dispatch selector three to the race results handler at $26FB.
Dispatch selector four to $116B for the car sales screen.
Initialise the music player, the run state, track availability, cash and the four condition values before showing the name prompt.
Six starting cash digits copied into $7342 by $0481. In this build they represent £20,000.
Reset all nine track flags starting at $0207.
X/Y supply a low/high pointer to 1000 VIC screen bytes followed by 1000 colour bytes. Copy them to $4000 and colour RAM at $D800, banking out I/O for the source reads.
Swap eight pages between $xx00, with the high byte in A, and the buffer addressed by X/Y. The caller uses this to put a different character set in the VIC display bank and preserve the previous set.
Read $0E and spin until the interrupt changes it.
Wait for X changes to $0E by calling $0523 once per count.
Preserve X and Y in immediate operands, use a carry-propagating byte mix over the low work area, and restore the registers before returning. The garage samples $0A afterward.
Patched with the X register before the byte mixer runs.
Patched with the Y register before the byte mixer runs.
Set CIA1 port A to input, read the active-low joystick lines from $DC00 and cache the raw byte in $0F.
Scan eight CIA1 keyboard rows against eight column masks. Write zero for pressed positions and $4C for released positions in the 64-byte array at $059B.
The selected CIA1 port B bit shifts left after each matrix position and returns to one on carry.
Active-low CIA1 port A row select, initialised to $FE and rotated after eight columns.
Initial storage for the 64 keyboard positions scanned at $0556.
Return the first pressed position through the conversion table at $FE6F and write $FF to $10 when every matrix position is released.
Clear the 1000 menu screen cells at $4000 and their corresponding colour RAM cells.
Divide A by repeated subtraction of 100, 10 and 1 and place the three digits in $063F through $0641.
The hundreds digit returned by the decimal conversion at $0614.
The tens digit left after subtracting hundreds and dividing the remainder by ten.
The residual units from the repeated-subtraction decimal conversion.
Install the IRQ and NMI vectors in high RAM, select the VIC bank at $4000, disable CIA interrupt sources, enable the VIC raster source and leave I/O visible with ROM banked out.
Patch the low and high operands at $06E1 and $06E2 from X and Y, then acknowledge any pending VIC interrupts before re-enabling CPU interrupts.

Save A, X, Y and the processor-port value. Map in I/O, acknowledge pending VIC causes and call the selected raster handler when bit zero is set. Restore the saved processor state and return from interrupt.
Low byte of the JSR target selected by each raster callback.
High byte of the IRQ callback that follows the fixed dispatcher.
Advance the sync byte at $0E and schedule raster line $FF while no screen-specific callback is selected.
Read joystick port 2, advance $0E and either silence the SID or call the RAM music player at $EC7F according to $023B.
If $023B is nonzero set SID volume to zero. Otherwise call the resident sequence driver.
Poll the bit-four sample in $0F until fire is pressed, then wait for it to be released.
Poll $0F until the sampled fire bit becomes one.
Switch to the dark transition callback at a raster boundary and disable the current screen's sprites.
Select the idle transition callback at $09C2 when the current raster reaches the menu split.
Wait for raster line $A4, switch the VIC character base to $5800 and schedule callback $0758 at line $E7.
The immediate D018 value written at the lower picture split. The car-specification display temporarily changes it.
At the lower raster split, switch the character base to $4800, update the stat bars and schedule $0799 at line $FF.
Select the upper picture charset, update joystick, music and sales office UI, scan the keyboard and schedule the lower picture split at $073C.
Acknowledge CIA1, apply the pending fine-scroll delta, re-enable interrupts, and compute and redraw the coarse viewport as needed.
Switch to HUD characters and hide the car sprites, wait through the lower display split, then schedule $0A77.
Start CIA1 timer interrupts, install the playfield's fine scroll and display bank, update the race clock, sprites and HUD, schedule $0A24, and sample joystick and audio.
Advance signed fine scroll in each selected direction. Crossing a character boundary adjusts the corresponding coarse camera coordinate and sets $24 for a redraw.
Measure the player position against the target screen position, clamp movement to three pixels per axis and stop scrolling beyond the track's configured bounds.
Refresh the viewport when $24 reports a coarse scroll change, then clear the flag.
Read 22 tile indices for each of 14 rows from the track chosen through $9C40. Expand each to 16 character codes and lay out the 88 by 56 character map starting at $8100.
Multiply the incoming tile ID by sixteen, add the dictionary base at $9440 and copy sixteen character bytes to four rows of the expanded map.
Updated from the tile index times sixteen plus the dictionary base, then advanced for each character copied.
High byte of the dictionary load at $0C54, adjusted by the tile calculation.
Within each group the indexes run backwards across a four-character row. The four row origins implement an 88-character stride with a high-byte correction in $0C60.
Derive the map-copy index from the coarse horizontal viewport state before entering the unrolled renderer.
Use the camera row and column to read the expanded map at $8100 and write the character viewport to the VIC screen at $4400.

Prepare the sales office screen, collect a name when required and dispatch the selected option from $0206. A negative selection identifies a track after masking bit seven.
Swap the sales office character sets into the VIC bank, load its screen and colours, print the class and track markers and select its raster callbacks.

Move the hand by one horizontal unit or two vertical units on an active-low direction and clamp its position at the edges of the menu.
Put the two pointer layers at the same position, give them separate colours and set the corresponding high X bits and sprite image pointers.
Draw the byte string from $02/$03 to the screen and colour pointers. A zero begins the next row, $FF ends the string and the byte at $0203 supplies the colour.
Translate hand coordinates to the coarse columns and rows used by the menu hit-box tables.
Restrict highlighting to the nine track rows and seven-column list. Select the corresponding colour address, reset other tracks and paint this row.
Low byte of the colour RAM store patched from the track row table at $1117.
High byte of the address of the track row whose colour is set to five.
Set seven cells of each track's menu row to colour seven before highlighting the current one.
Nine little-endian colour RAM targets for the track names.
Indexed high-byte reads for the track row targets starting at $1117.
While fire is held, search four-byte menu hit records by row and inclusive X interval. Copy the matching action byte to $0206, or clear it on no match.
Clear the dealer panel, print the refusal text, show the trade-in number and hold the screen until the menu reports its release action.
Draw the purchase response and its trade-in and cost values, restore the four car condition bytes to $FF, and wait for the release action.
Derive the asking price for the selected car, subtract the trade-in offer then subtract the balance from current cash digit by digit. Commit the result and clear carry when affordable.
Used to add ten modulo 256 after a decimal digit borrow from the trade-in adjustment.

Working six-digit balance before an accepted car purchase commits it.
Working six decimal digits of the asking price minus trade-in.
Send the calculated trade-in digits at $734E to the dealer panel's decimal display routine.
Draw the net sale amount from the working digits at $12F4.
Read a per-car base factor, derive an aggregate from the four condition bytes and repeatedly add the factor in decimal digits to calculate the offer.
Swap the picture character data, load the dealer screen and colour planes, print its opening message and install the dealer raster chain.
Build the availability flags for the variant rows and draw available car labels and their prices into successive display rows.
Append a pound mark and the variant's price digits to the dealer list row. The LDA at $14BF is patched to the selected car record.
Low byte of the feed from the active variant record's price digits.
High byte of the dealer list price source patched by the row renderer.
Availability flag for the first car row, filled from the current variant before drawing the list.
Availability flag for the second row in the dealer list.
Flag for the third variant's draw and highlight eligibility.
Per-row availability flag used for the fourth label and price row.
Flag controlling the fifth variant's presence in the drawn list.

Reset the colour of the dealer rows and recolour the eligible row under the pointer using a patched colour-RAM destination.
Patched from the selected row's colour pointer with four added for the inset.
High part of the colour RAM destination in the dealer highlight loop.
Low-byte indexed base for the seven colour RAM rows.
High-byte indexed base for the seven colour RAM row pointers.
Wait for a raster tick, then blank the text cells of the car sales panel and reset its initial colour rows.
Advance the cursor timer. Below its limit toggle both sprite enables periodically. At its limit enable the pointer and stop its automatic movement.
Counter incremented while the hand cursor is waiting for its timeout.
Draw the name prompt, run the keyboard input routine, then try three special-name handlers before clearing the prompt and rebuilding the HUD.
Copy the five loaded-code cash digits into the player cash balance.
Five replacement digits for the LOADED path, followed by a zero byte before the class setup.
Set class two, six cars and seven required laps, choose the associated variant and set the starting cash digit and class glyph.
Set class three, seven cars and nine required laps, then select its starting car, cash digit and class glyph.
Compare the entered name to the code text at the supplied table offset. Return carry set when the bytes match through the terminator.
Accept letters and spaces up to seven characters. Return or joystick fire ends input, Delete removes a character and a trailing asterisk terminates the comparison buffer.
Debounces the most recent translated scan code during name entry.
Character code written at the name cursor position on each pass.
Ten-step counter updated during name entry.
During name entry, step through raster lines in the lower band and change the VIC background colour for the prompt decoration.
Replace the centre panel and its colours, print the selected specification, wait for two fire cycles and restore the sales-office artwork.
Four pointers to the sales-office car specification text used by $17D3.
High-byte base of the word pointers for the selected specification.
Prepare the garage scene, poll menu input on raster ticks, then apply an available purchase after its cash check and refresh the HUD.
Stores the selected negative action's low seven bits before the price comparison.
Values copied into the twelve upgrade slots at $7354 when the purchase runs through $1862.
Load the garage screen and colours, draw item prices and the HUD, place the pointer and install the garage raster callback.
Convert four displayed item digits into the subtraction workspace and subtract them from current cash. Copy the new six digits back only on an affordable result.
Temporarily hold the digit after underflow so the subtraction can add ten and propagate the original borrow from the flags.
Six working cash digits for the garage price subtraction.
Two leading zero digits in the six-digit item price buffer.
The four selected price digits after removing the display encoding offset.
Clear sprite expansion, multicolour, priority and high X bits for the garage's own sprite setup.
When joystick fire is down and cursor X is in the right-hand exit range, publish the exit action.
Decrement the in-progress indicator timer and choose one of the two display tables when it crosses its threshold.
Countdown for the alternate indicator graphics drawn by $1968.
Scatter twelve selected character codes into the garage image using the cell offsets at $1997.
Twelve offsets from $40F3 for the garage indicator redraw.
Two twelve-byte alternatives copied to the indicator cells.
Reuse the upper sprite slots at subsequent raster lines to display the garage's item labels in several bands.
First available sprite slot for a band of the multiplexed garage labels.
Write a garage label's four-byte X, Y, image and colour record into the selected VIC sprite slot and enable it.
Slot whose position, image and colour are being written.
Twice the slot number for the VIC X/Y register pair.
Temporary carry from doubling the sprite's horizontal coordinate.
Walk twelve pointers to the price fields and write four digits per item. A price beginning with $FF draws the replacement codes for an unavailable item.
Current byte offset into the garage price cell pointer table.
Copy twelve packed decimal base prices, add a value drawn from the $1B9D table to each, and convert those bytes into four displayed digits per item.
Indexed start of the four-digit runtime price records. The leading digit also carries the unavailable marker $FF.
Second digit of the four-byte garage price record.
Third digit of each garage price record, generated from the high nibble of the low-price byte.
Indexed least-significant digit base. The other addresses within this range are adjacent slots in the runtime four-byte records.
Name setup writes $FF at this first digit to suppress the garage price for the ninth entry.
Runtime availability marker for the tenth price record.
Runtime availability marker for the eleventh price record.
Runtime availability marker for the twelfth price record.
Twelve two-byte packed decimal price seeds copied into the runtime price workspace.
Thirty-two little-endian packed decimal increments indexed by the low five bits of the sampled byte at $0A.
High-byte indexed base for the decimal increments starting at $1B9D.
Mark the chosen track as used, initialise track state and audio, run the starting sequence and enter the race update.
Run car state and input across sync ticks, update race results and condition, handle pause and repeat until a finish or failure transfers control to the results screen.
Last sync byte seen by the race vehicle and timer loop.
On a Space press, silence the audio, wait for release then for the next press before enabling the race sound again.
Select keyboard row $7F and test bit four in CIA1 port B. Store zero in $EC while Space is pressed and $FF when released.
Count with decimal addition, rolling the low and middle fields at $60 and incrementing the high field on the second carry.
Track the maximum sampled player speed in the results field at $1D33.
React to a new completed lap by queuing its sound and comparing the elapsed lap fields with the stored best.
Clear the decimal race tick fields and store the most recently seen completed lap.
Lower decimal elapsed-lap field copied to the best time when the comparison accepts it.
Upper decimal field of the elapsed time for the best lap comparison.
Cached player's completed lap count used to detect a change.
Maximum value of the player speed byte sampled during the race.
Return carry set when the player reaches the lap comparison, or when three selected rivals have all reached it.

Copy seven progress pairs to workspace. Compare each active rival against the player's lap and checkpoint pair, append rivals at least as far along in slot order, append slot zero and store the number ahead in $0213.
Patched to twice the number of active cars. The loop up to this bound compares each rival against the player.
First rival index qualifying for the finish check, in slot order rather than track order.
Second qualifying index in the rival list assembled by $1D74.
Third qualifying index in the rival list, followed by adjacent ranking state.
Indexed checkpoint byte of the interleaved progress pairs compared by $1D74.
Indexed lap byte of the interleaved progress pairs compared by $1D74.
Check fuel, engine, body and tyres in that order against four. On failure record the corresponding message index and set the finishing-place index to the last car.
Select CIA1 keyboard row $7F and read bit six for Q. Return carry set and force the final place to the field size minus one if pressed.
Restore the racing charsets, expand the selected track, initialise camera and car state, build the HUD and switch to the race raster handlers.
Set up the three repeated countdown pulses and the differently pitched final pulse, using waits measured by raster ticks.
Write zero across the SID voice and filter register span before starting the next countdown pulse.
Set the frequency and envelope of SID voice one, gate it for the count held at $1F11 and then release the gate.
Low SID pitch byte selected for the initial or final countdown sound.
High pitch byte paired with $1F0F.
Raster waits for which the countdown tone's gate remains open.
When nonzero the race effects callback returns immediately.
Set the display-state byte for track mode and prepare the initial per-race character attributes.
Select the current descriptor through the two-byte pointer table at $7F8D. Read the initial coarse scroll coordinates and their limits, then initialise the fine-scroll counters.

Read the starting heading, progress counters, target coordinates and seven starting positions from the descriptor. Apply purchased upgrades to the player car parameters and load the remaining track-list pointers.
Offset into the four-byte car configuration rows, advanced by four per initialised car.
Track's start heading for both the car sprite and its initial target heading.
Initial checkpoint value set in each active car's progress field.
Low byte of the starting X target copied to each car's $7512 field.
High byte of the starting X target copied to $751A.
Low byte copied to all initial Y target slots at $7522.
High byte copied into the corresponding $752A array.

Read four-byte replacement records through the final descriptor pointer. The first byte gates each record by class, the word gives the destination and the final byte starts a 3-by-3 sequence of consecutive character codes.
$20C7 updates this immediate compare operand to the current class plus one, controlling the cutoff of the ordered overlay list.
Nine offsets for the three-by-three replacement tiles installed by $20B8, using an 88-cell row stride.
Read three-byte mode and address records from the track. Write $FE markers in either paired vertical strips or paired horizontal rows until the negative byte terminates the list.
Invert the five low active-low joystick bits into the player's control byte when control is enabled. Pass stick up and down to the two missile handlers and update the player's special movement state.
Convert the coarse camera coordinates plus three cells to pixels and subtract the fine-scroll offsets. Return the two 16-bit screen origins in $48 through $4B.
Translate car positions into screen coordinates, assign visible objects to the low or high sprite slots, write X high bits and the priority mask and enable the sprites.
Subtract the viewport origin from the object's X and Y, reject off-screen positions, then choose a sprite slot path using the car's active flags.
Write an object's position, high X bit, colour and image pointer into the next free low-numbered sprite slot.
Write the object to the next free high-numbered sprite slot and set the background priority bit when the object's track flag requests it.
Run the speed-based accumulator, high-speed wear and collision-impulse wear updates.
Above the current top speed minus ten, add to the high-speed counter and subtract one from $735C every 32 counts.
Accumulates ticks over the near-top-speed threshold and controls deductions from $735C.
When the player has a nonzero collision impulse, decrement the condition byte $735E every 64 ticks of that condition.
Counts ticks during a collision impulse and gates the periodic wear.
Subtract speed from a 16-bit counter. Underflow deducts one from $735F and resets the high byte to $28.
Subtract player speed from this low byte and take its borrow into the high byte.
High accumulator byte reloaded with $28 after an underflow.
Apply the body-condition loss associated with an impact to the running player car state.
Counts collision calls when the body-protection option is set. The damage path uses its low two bits.
Clear both missile active flags and velocity state, then reset the up and down repeat counters to six.
Decrement the up counter and launch if the counter reaches zero, a front missile has been bought and the missile slot is free.
Mirror the front check for down. Set the heading offset to eight of sixteen directions and consume the rear missile before launch.

Copy the player position to object slot seven and pick a facing from the car heading plus the front/rear offset. Derive signed horizontal and vertical motion from the direction table and queue sound effect four.
Move an active missile, cycle its graphics and check cars and track surfaces. On a hit it advances an explosion sequence before clearing the active flags.
Test object slot seven against the other cars. If a collision is found start its explosion, queue the impact sound and clear the affected car control mask.
Snapshot the old position and heading, build signed 24-bit deltas from speed and the direction table, add them to fixed-point coordinates, then check contact and update car state.
Apply the collision impulse, scan overlapping cars and test road samples. On a blocking tile restore the saved position, stop the car and handle impact state.
Update the spin timer and facing, apply covered-area and checkpoint logic, then increase speed with fire or subtract three speed units on release. A separate timer gates turning.
Last XOR of the player's coordinate bytes for suppressing repeated impact sound and damage at the same position.
Prepare the results picture and music, wait for fire and apply the finishing result to the active class, money and next menu.
Incremented by the results path as it evaluates advancement.
Patch the completion text for the first class, draw it and reveal the class two password.
Patch the class-completion text for the second class and show the class three password.
Draw the two-line congratulation text from $7842.
Select a failure or track-complete message, print its two lines into the results view, then wait 200 raster ticks before tearing it down.
Zero between the return from the outcome display and the next text helper.
Print the selected name code until its asterisk marker or the field width, then enable blinking.
When enabled, XOR the colour of the six password cells on the chosen raster-counter boundary.
Left clear when there is no class password drawn, set by the password renderer to allow colour blinking.
Turn A into two consecutive character codes at the screen pointer and advance Y beyond them.
Swap result character data into the lower charset, load the result screen and colours, populate its text and select the result raster sequence.
Zero the border and background, hide sprites and select the result IRQ callback at line $DF.
Convert the race number, place, elapsed time, best lap and maximum speed to screen glyph pairs. The last calculation derives a numeric result from the saved speed and sampled variation.
Add the sampled variation to the result-dependent speed term when writing the second speed statistic.
Screen column offsets for the result time digits.
Index the prize table by class and rank, clamping rank to the fourth entry.
Patched to class times eight to select four prize pairs.
First digit base of the two-byte prize entries indexed by class and rank.
Indexed second digit of each prize pair within the class and position table.
Add the prize's decimal digits to player cash from right to left and carry between positions.
Clear two sprite work areas, enable eight aligned sprites and copy the GAME OVER source rows a few bytes at a time as raster ticks advance.
Number of sprite bytes exposed on the current pass of the GAME OVER animation.
Eight horizontal positions for the animated GAME OVER letters.
Copy the number of exposed bytes from a source GAME OVER sprite to the current destination slot.
The branch returns to the character-copy loop for each newly revealed byte.
Blank two HUD rows, print the menu headings, update cash, car name and condition bars and prepare the menu cursor text.
Wait for the raster value supplied in A before rebuilding the cash and condition rows.
Print speed, position, lap and condition labels, initialise the number displays and install character codes for the four bars.
Eight rows copied into character $2F of the HUD charset at $4978 during race setup.
Store zero in the 80 screen bytes addressed by the pointer at $11.
Refresh the speed display, print current place from $0213 and current lap from the player's entry at $74B2 and update the bars.
Copy fourteen display bytes of the current variant to the menu HUD and colour the field.
Write the pound glyph and cash digits with suppression of leading zeros, then clear the remainder of the field.
Tracks whether a nonzero digit has been drawn in the HUD cash field.
Copy the sixteen bar colours and preserve the supplied screen pointer for the stat bar writers.
Call the shared bar renderer four times with the saved condition bytes and the four HUD columns.
Divide the input byte by eight, translate it through $2CFA, then write whole, partial and empty bar cells.
Patched from the field's initial offset to limit the condition bar's screen writes.
Temporary fill level used to draw a particular condition bar.
Condition display conversion for the 32 groups obtained by shifting an eight-bit condition down by three.
Look up the active variant's record offset in $737D and return it in X.
Copy forty screen codes through the source pointer and set their matching colour cells to one.
Convert the player speed byte at $DC into whole and partial HUD bar cells, with eight speed units per fill increment.
A second return byte between the HUD speed writer and the alternate lookup at $2D72.
Convert car slot X to a map Y row and X character coordinate, then prepare an address for the corresponding expanded-map cell. The analysed direct calls use the newer lookup in $3EF3.
Patched from the X character coordinate in the retired cell-address lookup.

Destination offset within the HUD chosen for the body condition bar.
HUD column offset passed alongside the fuel condition at $735F.

Indexed Y component of the signed direction pairs at $2DEF.
Track 1 initialises coarse scroll at (29, 11) with bounds (44, 23). The rest holds start and progress settings, seven X/Y start positions and four list pointers.
